messages.subject: Rengine won't start-- StatET finds rj library but claims otherwise
messages.subject_clean: Rengine won't start-- StatET finds rj library but claims otherwise
messages.body_plain:
Hi there

I am trying to run Eclipse / StatET / R but am told that "Launching the R Console was cancelled, because it seems starting the R engine failed.". Google etc reveal lots of similar questions, but my error messages seem subtly different. Disclaimer: I have never used Eclipse before and don't know what I'm doing.

The rest of the summary message is "Please make sure that R package 'rj' (2.0 or compatible) is installed and that the R library paths are set correctly for the R environment configuration 'R-3.2.2patched'."

However, looking at the detailed error log, the system is managing to find 'rj' OK--- see below. I did install 'rj' (version 2.1.0-4) and 'rj.gd', and they can be loaded fine from a standard R session; I did have to add a "Java/jre1.8.0_51/bin/client" to my PATH before 'rj.gd' would load. FWIW I do get a warning from 'library(rj)' that 'rj' was built under R 3.2.3, but I get lots of those for other packages too... surely that should be no problem..?

My system is Windows 7, R 3.2.2 patched 32-bit, Java JRE 1.8.0_51, rj version 2.1.0-4, Eclipse Mars2 4.5.2, StatET up-to-date as of 7/3/2016 (I don't know how to find the installed version number for StatET).

Any advice appreciated! Further excerpts from detailed error log (which I redirected to file) below; it shows that parts of the rj package are indeed being found.

Mark Bravington

messages.subject: Re: Build statet from source
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tal,

[2016-03-15 18:55] Tal Hayon wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I'd really appreciate an explanation of how to build statet from source.
> I couldn't find one either on the site or in the mailing lsit.
>
> I've tried getting all the projects from github but I'm having trouble
> understanding what to run with maven and some pom.xml files have
> reference to a variable that's not defined anywhere - in short I'm
> really lost.

Do you mean the property "walware.repo.url.base"? You have to define it 
for your build. It is the base URL for P2 repositories with the 
dependencies. The required dependencies are listed in the parent pom 
'-build/pom.xml' (<repositories>) of each module.

The Maven builds of StatET and third party repositories are all started 
by building the 'releng' project with Maven profiles 'walware-releng' 
and the product specific profile (listed in pom.xml of releng).

For example to build the Lucene repository run Maven in releng:
 > mvn package -P walware-releng,3rdparty-lucene -Dwalware.repo.url.base=...

To build StatET (including Redocs) run Maven in releng:
 > mvn package -P walware-releng,statet,docmlet.tex,docmlet.wikitext 
-Dwalware.repo.url.base=...

Regards,
Stephan




>
> Thanks,
> Tal.
